q: How must flexible compression joints be made under the plumbing code?
o: With rubber strips cut and wrapped on site
With cement mortar packed around the pipe
With solder run into the gap
ref: 1999 Revised National Plumbing Code of the Philippines, Chapters 13–14
n: Compression joints rely on a gasket squeezed to an exact fit, so only factory-made, approved assemblies are allowed.

q: Which head do standard cleanout plugs have, so a wrench can turn them?
ref: 1999 Revised National Plumbing Code of the Philippines, Chapters 13–14
n: The raised square head takes a wrench. Plugs set flush in finished floors may have countersunk heads instead.

q: Which pipe materials may be joined with threaded (screwed) joints?
o: Copper tube, types M and DWV
Galvanized iron or steel, and plastic with enough wall
ref: 1999 Revised National Plumbing Code of the Philippines, Chapters 13–14
n: Threads need thick walls. Thin copper tube is soldered, and cast iron and clay use caulked or gasketed joints.

q: How is plastic pipe joined to pipe of another material?
o: With solvent cement applied to the metal
By heat-fusing the plastic onto the metal
With an approved transition fitting or adapter
ref: 1999 Revised National Plumbing Code of the Philippines, Chapters 13–14
n: Different materials expand and seal differently, so a listed adapter made for that pair is used.

q: What color marking identifies Type M copper tube?
ref: 1999 Revised National Plumbing Code of the Philippines, Chapters 13–14
n: Copper tube colors: K green (thickest), L blue, M red (thinnest pressure tube), DWV yellow.

q: What is the most lead allowed in solder and flux used on drinking-water piping?
ref: 1999 Revised National Plumbing Code of the Philippines, Chapters 13–14
n: Lead leaches into water, so 50/50 tin-lead solder is banned on potable lines. Lead-free solders are used instead.

q: Are fittings that obstruct flow allowed in drainage piping?
o: Yes, if a cleanout is placed upstream
Yes, if the pipe is 100 mm or larger
ref: 1999 Revised National Plumbing Code of the Philippines, Chapters 13–14
n: Anything that narrows or blocks a drain catches solids and causes stoppages.

q: Which piping is joined by soldering?
o: Copper and brass tubing, with approved flux
ref: 1999 Revised National Plumbing Code of the Philippines, Chapters 13–14
n: Soldering bonds metal to metal. Plastics are cemented or fused, and cast iron is caulked or clamped.

q: What must a closed cleanout plug be?
o: Vented, so sewer gas can escape
Loose, so it pops out under pressure
ref: 1999 Revised National Plumbing Code of the Philippines, Chapters 13–14
n: A cleanout opens into the drainage system, so its plug must seal against both water and sewer gas.

q: What color marking identifies Type K copper tube?
ref: 1999 Revised National Plumbing Code of the Philippines, Chapters 13–14
n: Type K has the thickest wall and is used underground and for high pressure.

q: What minimum flange face width does the plumbing code set for a water-closet flange?
ref: 1999 Revised National Plumbing Code of the Philippines, Chapters 13–14
n: The flange must be wide enough to take the closet bolts and bed the wax or gasket seal.

q: Where are cement-mortar joints on concrete pipe still allowed?
o: Only for repairs and connections to existing lines
ref: 1999 Revised National Plumbing Code of the Philippines, Chapters 13–14
n: Mortar joints are rigid and crack. New concrete pipe work uses rubber gasket joints.

q: What color marking identifies DWV copper tube?
ref: 1999 Revised National Plumbing Code of the Philippines, Chapters 13–14
n: DWV copper is thin-walled and made for drain, waste and vent lines, not pressure service.

q: Why is asbestos-cement pipe no longer used in new plumbing?
o: It cannot carry water under any pressure
Its fibers are a health hazard when it is cut or breaks down
It rusts quickly in wet soil
It is too heavy to lay in trenches
ref: 1999 Revised National Plumbing Code of the Philippines, Chapters 13–14
n: Old codes listed asbestos-cement pipe with rubber-ring couplings. Asbestos is now banned in new work.

q: How must a female-threaded connection be made on plastic pipe?
o: By cutting threads inside the pipe on site
By heating the pipe and pressing it onto a male thread
With a factory-made threaded fitting or adapter
By wrapping tape and forcing the pipe on
ref: 1999 Revised National Plumbing Code of the Philippines, Chapters 13–14
n: Threads cut on site inside plastic pipe weaken the wall and split. Only factory-made female threads are allowed.

q: Why is copper tubing not used for chemical or acid waste?
o: Copper is too heavy for waste lines
Copper cannot be soldered in waste lines
Copper is too rough inside for waste
ref: 1999 Revised National Plumbing Code of the Philippines, Chapters 13–14
n: Laboratory and chemical waste goes in resistant pipe such as borosilicate glass, polypropylene or high-silicon iron.

q: What marking must plumbing pipe and fittings carry?
o: The maker's name or mark and the standard it meets
The date the building permit was issued
The name of the building owner
ref: 1999 Revised National Plumbing Code of the Philippines, Chapters 13–14
n: Factory marks let the inspector confirm that the material is approved.

q: In a water test of water-supply piping, what pressure is applied?
ref: 1999 Revised National Plumbing Code of the Philippines, Chapters 13–14
n: The line is held at working pressure plus 50% and checked for leaks before it is covered.

q: In a push-fit (pressure-lock) joint, how is the pipe fitted?
o: It is threaded before it is pushed in
It is solvent-cemented into the socket
It is pushed in to the depth set by the maker
It is heat-fused into the socket
ref: 1999 Revised National Plumbing Code of the Philippines, Chapters 13–14
n: The grip ring and O-ring only hold and seal if the pipe reaches the full marked depth.

q: Why are threaded drainage fittings made with a built-in angle?
o: So pipes can be vented without a vent fitting
So the joints need no compound
So the pipe stays perfectly level
So pipes fall at about 2% toward the drain
ref: 1999 Revised National Plumbing Code of the Philippines, Chapters 13–14
n: Drainage fittings are tapped so that a straight pipe screwed in slopes about 2% (1:50).

q: Which pipes follow iron pipe size (IPS) dimensions?
o: Copper tube types K, L and M
ref: 1999 Revised National Plumbing Code of the Philippines, Chapters 13–14
n: IPS sizes match the old wrought-iron standard. Copper tube and soil pipe have their own size systems.

q: What is the shower pan (safe pan) under a site-built shower for?
o: A trap that seals the drain against sewer gas
A watertight liner that catches water leaking through the floor finish
A tray for storing soap and shampoo
A removable cover for the floor drain
ref: 1999 Revised National Plumbing Code of the Philippines, Chapters 13–14
n: Tile and grout let water through. The pan below sends it to the drain. Old codes used sheet lead; today PVC or CPE sheet is used.

q: How is a bell-and-spigot cast iron joint caulked?
o: Sealed with a rubber sleeve and steel clamp
Packed with oakum or hemp and filled with molten lead
ref: 1999 Revised National Plumbing Code of the Philippines, Chapters 13–14
n: The oakum centers the spigot and seals first. The lead is then caulked tight with a caulking iron.

q: At what temperature is brazing done?
o: 449°C and above, below the melting point of the metals
ref: 1999 Revised National Plumbing Code of the Philippines, Chapters 13–14
n: Brazing uses filler metals that melt above 449°C. It is stronger than soldering but still does not melt the pipe.

q: Which connections are NOT counted as slip joints?
o: Joints with a friction ring and nut
ref: 1999 Revised National Plumbing Code of the Philippines, Chapters 13–14
n: Slip joints are the nut, washer and friction-ring joints on trap and tailpiece connections. Ground, flared and ferrule joints are rigid.

q: How is a building sewer tested?
o: It is pressurized with air to 700 kPa
The ends are plugged and it is filled with water from the lowest to the highest point
Peppermint oil is poured into the vent
It is flushed once with a garden hose
ref: 1999 Revised National Plumbing Code of the Philippines, Chapters 13–14
n: A water test shows any leak by a drop in level. The sewer must stay full long enough to be inspected.

q: What must the flap of a backwater valve do at low flow?
o: Close fully to stop sewer gas
Lock shut until reset by hand
Stay open enough to let low flows pass
ref: 1999 Revised National Plumbing Code of the Philippines, Chapters 13–14
n: The valve closes only when sewage backs up. At normal low flow it must not hold back waste.

q: What material is the body of a drainage valve 102 mm and larger made of?
ref: 1999 Revised National Plumbing Code of the Philippines, Chapters 13–14
n: Large valve bodies are cast iron. Smaller ones, under 102 mm, are cast brass or bronze.

q: What plastic pipe may be threaded?
o: Schedule 80, with factory-cut or molded threads
Any schedule, as long as it is taped
ref: 1999 Revised National Plumbing Code of the Philippines, Chapters 13–14
n: Threads cut away part of the wall, so only thick Schedule 80 pipe may be threaded.

q: What type of gate valve is used in drainage piping?
o: Butterfly type with a narrow bore
ref: 1999 Revised National Plumbing Code of the Philippines, Chapters 13–14
n: A full-way valve leaves the whole pipe bore open, so solids pass without catching.

q: Before they are installed, what must plumbing fittings, including zinc-alloy parts, do?
o: Be approved by the owner in writing
Be imported from the United States
Meet an approved standard or listing
Be painted with an anti-rust coat
ref: 1999 Revised National Plumbing Code of the Philippines, Chapters 13–14
n: Every material must meet a recognized standard. Zinc alloys can corrode, so they must be listed for plumbing use.

q: How must the end of a water-closet stub be cut before the flange is set?
ref: 1999 Revised National Plumbing Code of the Philippines, Chapters 13–14
n: A square cut lets the flange seat evenly, so the closet sits level and seals.

q: What seals a compression-type (hub and gasket) cast iron joint?
o: A neoprene gasket in the hub
A stainless clamp and rubber sleeve
ref: 1999 Revised National Plumbing Code of the Philippines, Chapters 13–14
n: The spigot is pushed into a gasketed hub. It is faster than lead caulking and still flexible.

q: What material is the body of a drainage valve smaller than 102 mm made of?
ref: 1999 Revised National Plumbing Code of the Philippines, Chapters 13–14
n: Small valve bodies are brass or bronze. From 102 mm up, cast iron is used.

q: How deep must the lead be in a caulked cast iron joint?
ref: 1999 Revised National Plumbing Code of the Philippines, Chapters 13–14
n: One inch of lead, caulked tight over oakum, makes the joint.

q: May chemical leak-sealing additives be put into a plumbing system to stop leaks?
o: Yes, if a Master Plumber approves
ref: 1999 Revised National Plumbing Code of the Philippines, Chapters 13–14
n: Additives hide leaks and can contaminate water. Leaking joints must be remade.

q: When air is used instead of water to test water-supply piping, what pressure is applied?
ref: 1999 Revised National Plumbing Code of the Philippines, Chapters 13–14
n: The air test is held with no drop in pressure. Plastic pipe makers may forbid air tests.

q: How is a flared joint made?
o: The tube is soldered into a socket
The copper tube end is expanded with a flaring tool and clamped by a nut
A ferrule is squeezed onto the tube
The tube is pushed into an O-ring fitting
ref: 1999 Revised National Plumbing Code of the Philippines, Chapters 13–14
n: The flared end seats against a cone-shaped fitting. It is used on soft copper where soldering is not wanted.

q: What is a burned lead joint?
o: Lead poured into a cast iron hub over oakum
Solder wiped around the pipe with a cloth
Lead pipe fused by heat, with the weld at least as thick as the pipe
Lead pipe joined with a brass ferrule
ref: 1999 Revised National Plumbing Code of the Philippines, Chapters 13–14
n: Burning is welding lead to lead with a torch. The weld must not be thinner than the pipe wall.

q: What minimum outside diameter does the plumbing code set for a water-closet flange?
ref: 1999 Revised National Plumbing Code of the Philippines, Chapters 13–14
n: The flange must be big enough to cover the floor opening and hold the closet bolts.

q: At what temperature is soldering done?
ref: 1999 Revised National Plumbing Code of the Philippines, Chapters 13–14
n: Soldering uses fillers that melt below 427°C. Above 449°C it is called brazing.

q: How is copper water tube joined?
o: With compatible fittings, soldered or brazed
ref: 1999 Revised National Plumbing Code of the Philippines, Chapters 13–14
n: Copper tube walls are too thin to thread, so capillary fittings are soldered or brazed.

q: What does the code require of expansion joints in piping?
o: They must be buried in concrete
They must be locked with set screws
They must be accessible and free to move
They must be packed with lead
ref: 1999 Revised National Plumbing Code of the Philippines, Chapters 13–14
n: An expansion joint only works if it can move, and it must be reachable for inspection.

q: What minimum wall thickness must lead bends and traps have?
ref: 1999 Revised National Plumbing Code of the Philippines, Chapters 13–14
n: Lead is soft, so bends and traps need at least 1/8 in (3.2 mm) of wall.

q: What minimum width must the colored stripe on marked copper tube have?
ref: 1999 Revised National Plumbing Code of the Philippines, Chapters 13–14
n: The continuous color stripe (green, blue, red or yellow) is at least 1/4 in (6.4 mm) wide.

q: How is copper tube joined to threaded steel pipe?
o: By cutting threads on the copper tube
With a brass adapter sweated onto the copper
ref: 1999 Revised National Plumbing Code of the Philippines, Chapters 13–14
n: The brass adapter is soldered to the copper and screwed onto the steel. A dielectric union also stops galvanic corrosion.

q: How is lead pipe joined to iron or steel pipe?
o: With a caulking ferrule, soldering nipple or bushing
With a wiped joint directly to the iron
ref: 1999 Revised National Plumbing Code of the Philippines, Chapters 13–14
n: The brass ferrule or nipple is wiped to the lead and caulked or screwed into the iron.

q: How is hubless cast iron pipe joined?
o: With a rubber sleeve and a stainless-steel clamp and shield
ref: 1999 Revised National Plumbing Code of the Philippines, Chapters 13–14
n: The sleeve seals and the band clamp holds it. Hubless joints are quick and a little flexible.

q: Is enlarging a 76 mm closet bend to 102 mm counted as an obstruction?
o: Only if no cleanout is added
Only in buildings over three storeys
ref: 1999 Revised National Plumbing Code of the Philippines, Chapters 13–14
n: An enlargement in the direction of flow does not catch solids, so the code allows it.

q: What seals an elastomeric-gasket (push-on) joint?
o: A rubber O-ring or ring gasket compressed in the bell
ref: 1999 Revised National Plumbing Code of the Philippines, Chapters 13–14
n: The spigot is lubricated and pushed through the gasket, which seals by compression.

q: What is a wiped joint?
o: Lead fused by a torch into a weld
Oakum and lead poured into a hub
A lead joint made by wiping molten solder around the pipe with a cloth pad
A brass ferrule caulked into cast iron
ref: 1999 Revised National Plumbing Code of the Philippines, Chapters 13–14
n: Wiping is an old skill for joining lead pipe. The plumber shapes the hot solder into a smooth bulb.

q: What does solvent cement do in a plastic pipe joint?
o: Forms a separate glue film between the parts
Softens and fuses the pipe and fitting surfaces together
ref: 1999 Revised National Plumbing Code of the Philippines, Chapters 13–14
n: The solvent dissolves the surfaces, which weld into one piece as it evaporates.

q: What makes up a slip joint?
o: A compression nut, washer and friction ring
A ferrule forced onto the tube
A flared tube end and nut
A threaded union with a ground seat
ref: 1999 Revised National Plumbing Code of the Philippines, Chapters 13–14
n: Slip joints join trap arms and tailpieces, and they can be undone by hand. They must be accessible.

q: How are flanged fixture connections made?
o: With corrosion-resistant bolts and an approved gasket, washer or setting compound
ref: 1999 Revised National Plumbing Code of the Philippines, Chapters 13–14
n: The gasket or compound seals the flange, and the bolts must not rust away.

q: What color marking identifies Type L copper tube?
ref: 1999 Revised National Plumbing Code of the Philippines, Chapters 13–14
n: Type L is the usual choice for water supply inside buildings.

q: How is vitrified clay sewer pipe joined today?
ref: 1999 Revised National Plumbing Code of the Philippines, Chapters 13–14
n: Factory-applied gaskets replaced the old mortar joints, which cracked and let roots in.

q: How many bolts or screws, at least, fasten a water-closet flange under the code?
ref: 1999 Revised National Plumbing Code of the Philippines, Chapters 13–14
n: The flange is fastened down firmly so the closet cannot rock and break the seal.

q: What is a molded rubber coupling used for?
o: Joining pipes of different materials or sizes
Joining two copper tubes with solder
ref: 1999 Revised National Plumbing Code of the Philippines, Chapters 13–14
n: The rubber bushing takes up the difference in outside diameter between, for example, clay and plastic pipe.

q: How does a compression fitting seal?
o: A flared end is pressed onto a cone
Solder is drawn into a socket
A ferrule is squeezed onto the tube by a nut
A rubber sleeve is clamped around the pipe
ref: 1999 Revised National Plumbing Code of the Philippines, Chapters 13–14
n: Tightening the nut crushes the brass ferrule onto the tube. It is common at fixture supply stops.

q: Where are mechanical joints allowed?
o: On compatible cast iron systems, where approved
ref: 1999 Revised National Plumbing Code of the Philippines, Chapters 13–14
n: Mechanical (gasket and gland) joints are used on cast iron where they are listed for it.

q: What seals a vent pipe where it passes through the roof?
o: A flashing (roof jack) sealed to the roof and the pipe
ref: 1999 Revised National Plumbing Code of the Philippines, Chapters 13–14
n: Old codes used sheet lead flashings. Today neoprene or metal roof jacks are common.

q: Where is pipe-joint compound applied on a threaded joint?
ref: 1999 Revised National Plumbing Code of the Philippines, Chapters 13–14
n: Compound on the female threads gets pushed into the pipe, where it can foul water or catch solids.
